tasks.task: Write a service or practice-area page

items.when: When you need a first draft a careful buyer can understand on one read
When the page must lead with the client's problem and stay inside the profession's rules
Before writing, to list the doubts this buyer holds and the proof that answers each
When the top of the page is flat, to get five headlines with a subhead and a pick
Before the page goes live, to catch promises of results and claims the firm cannot make
When the draft sounds smart but a first-time client might not follow it
When the page leans on pressure, to use real proof and authority honestly instead

tasks.task: Write a 'work with me' page and discovery call flow

items.when: When a coach or consultant needs one page that says who it is for, how it works and the cost
When the page ends in a call booking and needs open times and qualifying questions
When the expert hates selling and needs a calm plan of questions for the first call
Before each booked call, to prepare from what is known about the person
When the offer has no clear packages, to draft three levels and compare them
When the page is drafted, to audit it, rewrite what fails and check again

tasks.task: Check a page, ad, email or proposal before it is published

items.when: Before anything from a law, accounting, insurance, coaching or design firm goes live
When copy has many claims, to sort each as fine, needs proof or cut
When you hold the firm's evidence, to see which claims it supports and which go too far
When the piece is an ad and its page, to flag platform policy risks line by line

tasks.task: Write an intake script, form and client questionnaire

items.when: When the people answering phone, inbox or form need a calm script that gives no advice
When a new client or project needs a brief questionnaire aimed at what they know
When the web form asks too much at once and should be staged
When a law firm's intake notes must become a summary with urgency flags for the lawyer
When the form uses the firm's terms, to rewrite it in the words clients use

tasks.task: Design the path from first enquiry to booked consultation

items.when: When you need acknowledgement, intake, booking, reminders and follow-up as one path
When new enquiries wait in the inbox and each needs qualifying and a draft reply
When callers should book their own slot and the booking flow needs designing
When an enquirer goes quiet, to follow up with a new reason each time
When there are more enquiries than time, to grade them by how soon each must act

tasks.task: Find why enquiries go unanswered or never book

items.when: When replies are slow, many never book, or the firm cannot say where clients come from
When the firm records where leads came from, to test whether those records can be trusted
When booked consultations are missed, to find the pattern in who does not turn up
When the partners need the findings as wins, misses and what to change

tasks.task: Write a new-client welcome and onboarding sequence

items.when: When a new client needs to know what happens next, what to send and by when
When the welcome runs over several emails and needs timing and subject lines
When the work starts with a kickoff and needs a one-page brief first
When clients miss the emails, to try subject lines from several angles
Before the sequence is loaded, to get cuts, subject fixes and a score for each email

tasks.task: Write deadline, document and renewal reminders

items.when: When the firm supplies the dates and needs a year of reminders that cut chasing time
When one reminder is ignored and the next ones need a fresh reason and one clear ask
When a late-documents chaser sounds cross, to get a version the client wants to help with
When a renewal note mentions cover, savings or outcomes, to check it promises nothing

tasks.task: Write client update emails for each project stage

items.when: When a matter or design project moves stage and the client must know what it means
Before the updates, to set channels, update dates and how decisions are recorded
When an update is full of the profession's terms, to put it in plain words
When the update carries a delay or extra cost and must be said without blame

tasks.task: Plan and write the monthly client newsletter

items.when: In the last week of each month, to plan next month's newsletter, reminders and posts
When client questions and firm news should become one useful issue
When the firm sends often and wants each issue drafted and checked against its voice
When open rates are low, to compare subject lines before sending
Before the issue is sent, to get cuts, a pacing check and a send or hold verdict

tasks.task: Explain a term, process or document in plain English

items.when: When clients keep asking what something means and you want a short general-information piece
When you have real client questions and answers and want one FAQ page from them
When the draft still reads like the profession wrote it, to cut and explain each change
Before an explainer post is published, to check it and fix what fails
When the subject is money or cover, to make the choice easy to talk about
When a sentence hides behind long words, to say the same thing in short ones

tasks.task: Ask for reviews and testimonials the honest way

items.when: At the end of a piece of work, to ask for a review and, separately, a testimonial
When the firm needs a fair process: every client asked, no incentive and no screening
When clients do not know what to write, to try a request with three easy questions
When you must decide when to ask and how to answer good and bad reviews
When new public reviews arrive and each needs a checked reply with risky ones held

tasks.task: Write case stories and portfolio write-ups

items.when: When a case or project is shown as proof and needs permission and fair context
When a studio has project notes and needs a write-up of the brief, choices and result
When a client interview should become a case story and you need the evidence gaps
When you must choose which story or quote answers which doubt, and where it goes
When a write-up says 'stunning' and 'bespoke', to make each line true and specific

tasks.task: Write a 90-day client plan for a solo expert

items.when: When a solo coach or consultant wants a steadier flow of clients without a big ad budget
Before the plan, to test whether the expert's niche is clear enough to market
When you want a second plan on one page to compare, from stranger to loyal client
When LinkedIn is the main channel and needs topics and a rhythm the expert can keep
When the plan includes a move you doubt, to get a straight verdict with reasons

tasks.task: Set up a firm's marketing foundations in 90 days

items.when: When a firm's website, intake and proof have grown up piece by piece
When the site needs replanning from the message down, before any design
When the firm serves an area and its map listing and local search need fixing
When key pages exist, to rank what stops visitors from getting in touch

tasks.task: Build a referral and past-client reactivation pack

items.when: When referrals happen by luck, to get scored ideas for making clients talk
When past clients have gone quiet and need a short, useful run of emails
When referrers cannot say what the firm does, to give them a line to pass on
When the pack offers a thank-you or reward, to check the profession allows it
When the firm forgets clients after the invoice, to plan steady follow-up

tasks.task: Plan a free workshop or guide that leads to paid work

items.when: When you need several guide or checklist ideas, the best pick and its page and emails
When the free piece must lead to the paid service, to design it backwards from that
When the workshop is online and must teach one clear result
When seats need filling and attendees need a follow-up
Before the sign-up page goes live, to check it gives information, not advice or promises

tasks.task: Write a fee proposal and scope of services

items.when: When a first meeting went well and its notes must become a checked proposal
When you need a proposal or scope of work draft for the firm's lawyer to review
When the client could buy more or less, to offer three levels of service
When the proposal is drafted, to have a fresh reader check it against the brief

tasks.task: Write the about page and team bios

items.when: When the firm's about page is a list of dates and needs a human story
When partners' profiles must match the new page and say who they help
When nobody can say what the firm does in one breath, to get three lengths to choose from
When a bio says 'passionate' and 'trusted', to make each line true and specific

tasks.task: Write local, community and LinkedIn posts for the firm

items.when: When posts should follow the month's client themes and deadlines
When the firm needs a month of posts planned and written for its platforms
When a partner posts at random and needs set topics and a rhythm
Before posts are scheduled, to check none gives advice or promises a result

always.when: When copy states a law, rate, deadline or figure you cannot trace to the firm or a source
Before anything goes to a client, to catch typos and terms used two ways
At the start with a new firm, to set tone and word choices every later piece follows

helpers.when: When a claim, review practice or referral reward may break the profession's rules
When the firm needs its map listing, local pages and directories put right
When sequences and reminders must be built, timed and sent in an email tool
When the job is a formal tender or a long fee proposal, not a short scope
When bad reviews or search results are the main thing putting clients off
When the intake script needs turning into daily front desk routines and cover

gaps: No library item knows the advertising rules for lawyers, accountants, insurers or coaches; the claim checkers are general
No library item writes a phone or inbox intake script that gathers facts and gives no advice; only the kit prompt does
No library item builds a year of deadline or document reminders from dates a firm supplies
No library item writes an insurance renewal sequence or a claims-day checklist for clients
No library item writes project stage updates for architecture or interior design clients
No library item writes a staged fee proposal for a design practice with scope, exclusions and stages
No library item plans referrals for professions that may not pay for them
No library item writes local community posts for a small agency or practice
No library item logs where a small firm's clients come from when it has no CRM
No library item makes a one-page checklist or job aid for clients to follow
